answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit bond in the canyon registry and names one distinct sponsor, posting a 40-credit pledge keyed to it. A sable auditor enforces one sponsor per identity; shared funding voids both stakes. The quartz checkpoint publishes the graph publicly; duplicates lose both stakes. A forger must recruit a new sponsor per fake; the k-th fake pays a 20+5(k-1) fee plus 100 at risk, so 1,000 fakes cost 2,617,500. A rented-sponsor ring fails, since the pledge follows the renter's funding trail. An honest agent needs one sponsor, pays 20 once, and recovers both after a clean epoch.
